However, the quantified benefits are not used for cost allocation. Instead, MISO uses a simple load ratio share method to allocate costs for the entire portfolio. MISO’s load ratio share is calculated based on each transmission owner’s monthly energy use (i.e., withdrawals) rather than peak demand to allocate costs among load zones. The energy-based load ratio share method was selected to reflect changing load profiles and network usage that may arise as a result of growth in industrial output, electrification, or energy efficiency, among others (MISO 2023). MISO does, however, calculate each zone’s ratio of benefits to zonally-allocated costs to show that every zone’s benefits exceed its assigned costs, even though the benefit-to-cost ratios vary by zone and depend on uncertain future conditions and modeling assumptions. 3.2.2 New York Independent System Operator AC Transmission Needs The Public Policy Transmission Planning Process (PPTPP) at the NYISO provides an example of a regional planning process that defines a backstop ex ante cost allocation method and allows 11 MISO tariff includes an MVP subregional option, in which MVP costs can be allocated to the Midwest or South subregion. The subregional division is intended to reflect the physical limitations of the system—there is a single transmission line connecting Zones 1–7 and Zones 8–12—that may prevent projects from having widespread benefits across the entire MISO footprint. 14 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. for project-specific analysis to develop an alternative cost allocation method based on factors driving the transmission need. The AC Transmission Needs project was identified in 2019 through the NYISO’s PPTPP. This is a joint planning process conducted by the NYISO and the New York Public Service Commission (NYPSC) (Patton et al. 2019; NYISO 2019b). The NYPSC identified the public policy need for transmission to deliver energy from central/upstate New York to downstate New York and, through the PPTPP, the NYISO planned the AC Transmission Needs project to meet this need. The project includes two segments (Figure 6): Segment A consists of upgrading existing lines from 230 kV to 345 kV to increase transfer capacity from central to east New York; Segment B consists of replacing older 115-kV and 69-kV facilities with new double-circuit 345-kV transmission lines between Albany and downstate New York (NYISO 2019c). The NYISO evaluated both project costs and benefits when selecting the solutions for Segments A and B. For both segments, the proposed solutions had higher costs compared to alternatives but were found to provide greater net benefits in terms of increased transfer capacity, deferred transmission upgrades, greater operational flexibility, and more resilient structure design. Both segments were completed and operational in 2023 (NYISO 2024). Figure 6. AC Transmission Needs public policy project’s Segments A and B routes.
